newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-HARRODS OWNER BUYS CONTROL OF FULHAM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HARRODS OWNER BUYS CONTROL OF FULHAM.

text.p: Mohamed Al Fayed, owner of top London department store Harrods, plans to invest 30 million pounds ($49 million) in English second division soccer club Fulham, a Harrods spokesman said on Thursday.
Millionaire businessman Al Fayed is taking over as chairman of the London club after agreeing to acquire a controlling stake.
The financial backing has allowed Fulham to repurchase the freehold to their Craven Cottage stadium on the banks of the river Thames in west London for an estimated 7.5 million pounds.
Egyptian-born businessman Al Fayed has promised funds to acquire players and improve and develop a stadium which the club has occupied for a century.
Craven Cottage is only a few minutes' drive from the world renowned Harrods store in Knightsbridge.

Al Fayed's Fulham Leisure Holdings company and the Muddyman family, the other shareholders, want to increase the capacity of the stadium from its present 15,000 to 25,000. An earlier plan for a residential development as part of a revamped stadium has been shelved.

Al Fayed promised to work to restore the fortunes of Fulham, a club which has spent most of its existence in the lower divisions of the English game. Fulham were recently promoted from the third division, the bottom rung on the professional ladder.
"I am totally committed, both personally and financially, to the plans for the revival of the club and I look forward to sharing a bright future with the loyal fans," he said.
